faqs.q: What are the Dinamic Oil NP and NPA compact hydraulic winches used for?
faqs.a: The NP and NPA compact hydraulic winches are small hoisting winches with a planetary gearbox inside the drum, 6 models with first-layer line pull of 500 to 1,650 daN on 6 to 10 mm rope. They are built in Italy by Dinamic Oil.

faqs.q: How do I read the NP and NPA winch model names such as NP05 and NPA19?
faqs.a: The model name is the series plus the size: NP05, NP08, NP10 and NP12 are the NP models, and NPA18 and NPA19 the NPA models (NP05 is 500 daN, NPA19 is 1,650 daN). Indus part numbers follow, such as IH-DO-NP-05 and IH-DO-NPA-19.

faqs.q: What sizes and line pulls do the Dinamic Oil NP and NPA compact hydraulic winches come in?
faqs.a: There are 6 models with first-layer line pull of 500 to 1,650 daN. Examples: NP05 (500 daN, 6 mm rope), NP08 (800 daN, 7 mm rope), NP10 (1,100 daN, 8 mm rope), NP12 (1,300 daN, 8 mm rope), NPA18 (1,500 daN, 10 mm rope), NPA19 (1,650 daN, 10 mm rope). The size table gives each model’s rope, motor displacement, oil flow, pressure, gear ratio, brake torque and weight.

faqs.q: Is the line pull of the Dinamic Oil NP and NPA compact hydraulic winches at the first or last layer?
faqs.a: The table gives the first-layer pull, the highest the winch delivers, and it is 500 to 1,650 daN across the series. Pull falls and rope speed rises as the rope builds up on the drum, and the maker’s datasheet gives both for every layer.

faqs.q: What is the construction and brake of the Dinamic Oil NP and NPA compact hydraulic winches?
faqs.a: A hydraulic motor with a pilot-operated lowering control valve holds the load on the way down, and a negative multi-disc brake of steel and bronze discs, closed by springs and opened by the hoisting pressure, locks the drum whenever the motor stops. The planetary reduction is oil-bath lubricated, with marine-grade paint as standard.

faqs.q: What standard and class rating apply to the Dinamic Oil NP and NPA compact hydraulic winches?
faqs.a: They are classified to UNI ISO 4301/1, mechanism class M4 to M6 (NP) and M4 to M5 (NPA), and every winch is load-tested above its rated pull before dispatch. A class certificate (ABS, DNV, LR, BV) is available on request.

faqs.q: What hydraulic circuit do the Dinamic Oil NP and NPA compact hydraulic winches need?
faqs.a: For the Dinamic Oil NP and NPA compact hydraulic winches, use an open-centre directional valve, a relief valve, and a return line with 1 to 5 bar back pressure, with the drain connected directly to tank where the winch has one. Filter the oil to 10 micron (25 micron at most) and run the winch unloaded at full flow for five minutes before the first lift.

faqs.q: What safety rules apply when installing the Dinamic Oil NP and NPA compact hydraulic winches?
faqs.a: On the Dinamic Oil NP and NPA compact hydraulic winches, keep at least four wraps of rope on the drum and the return-line back pressure under 5 bar. Hoisting is counterclockwise viewed from the motor side (clockwise is built to order), so never swap the hoses to reverse it. Not for lifting people unless built to a man-riding specification.

faqs.q: What accessories and options can be fitted to the Dinamic Oil NP and NPA compact hydraulic winches?
faqs.a: Options include a rope tensioner (B), lowering limit switches (C1, C2), a strain-gauge load limiter (D), load cells (E), rotary limit switches (F1, F2) and the ELD system. Grooved drums and man-riding brakes are built to order. See the [hydraulic winch accessories](/p/dinamic-oil-hydraulic-winch-accessories) listing for what each code does.

See our [planetary gearbox oil in hot climates guide](/blog/planetary-gearbox-oil-in-hot-climates).

faqs.q: What are the Dinamic Oil SRD heavy hydraulic winches used for?
faqs.a: The SRD heavy hydraulic winches are built on the maker’s WD planetary winch drives with bent-axis axial piston motors, with first-layer pull of 8,000 to 29,700 daN on 18 to 32 mm rope. They suit duties such as crawler-crane hoists.

faqs.q: How do I read the SRD winch model names such as SRD A60 and SRD G230 (on request)?
faqs.a: The model name is SRD plus a frame letter and size: SRD A60 is 8,000 daN and SRD G230 is 29,700 daN. E150, F180 and G230 are built on request. Examples are IH-DO-SRD-A60 and IH-DO-SRD-G230.

faqs.q: What sizes and line pulls do the Dinamic Oil SRD heavy hydraulic winches come in?
faqs.a: There are 7 models with first-layer line pull of 8,000 to 29,700 daN. Examples: SRD A60 (8,000 daN, 18 mm rope), SRD C100 (13,000 daN, 22 mm rope), SRD E150 (on request) (19,400 daN, 26 mm rope), SRD G230 (on request) (29,700 daN, 32 mm rope). The size table gives each model’s rope, motor displacement, oil flow, pressure, gear ratio, brake torque and weight.

faqs.q: Is the line pull of the Dinamic Oil SRD heavy hydraulic winches at the first or last layer?
faqs.a: The table gives the first-layer pull, the highest the winch delivers, and it is 8,000 to 29,700 daN across the series. Pull falls and rope speed rises as the rope builds up on the drum, and the maker’s datasheet gives both for every layer.

faqs.q: What is the construction and brake of the Dinamic Oil SRD heavy hydraulic winches?
faqs.a: A bent-axis axial piston motor with a pilot-operated lowering control valve holds the load on the way down, and a negative multi-disc brake locks the drum whenever the motor stops. A hydraulic limit switch for hoisting and lowering is fitted. Planetary reduction is oil-bath lubricated.

faqs.q: What standard and class rating apply to the Dinamic Oil SRD heavy hydraulic winches?
faqs.a: They are classified to UNI ISO 4301/1, mechanism class M5 to M7, and every winch is load-tested above its rated pull before dispatch. A class certificate (ABS, DNV, LR, BV) is available on request.

faqs.q: What hydraulic circuit do the Dinamic Oil SRD heavy hydraulic winches need?
faqs.a: For the Dinamic Oil SRD heavy hydraulic winches, use an open-centre directional valve, a relief valve, and a return line with 1 to 5 bar back pressure, with the drain connected directly to tank where the winch has one. Filter the oil to 10 micron (25 micron at most) and run the winch unloaded at full flow for five minutes before the first lift.

faqs.q: What safety rules apply when installing the Dinamic Oil SRD heavy hydraulic winches?
faqs.a: On the Dinamic Oil SRD heavy hydraulic winches, keep at least four wraps of rope on the drum and the return-line back pressure under 5 bar. Hoisting is counterclockwise viewed from the motor side (clockwise is built to order), so never swap the hoses to reverse it. Not for lifting people unless built to a man-riding specification.

faqs.q: What accessories and options can be fitted to the Dinamic Oil SRD heavy hydraulic winches?
faqs.a: Options are a rope tensioner, lowering limit switches, rotary limit switches and the ELD electronic load detection system. The strain-gauge pull limiters are not available on SRD; see our [crane winch load monitoring guide](/blog/crane-winch-load-monitoring). See the [hydraulic winch accessories](/p/dinamic-oil-hydraulic-winch-accessories) listing for what each code does.

faqs.q: How do the Dinamic Oil SRD heavy hydraulic winches compare with the nearest series?
faqs.a: The SRD covers 8,000 to 29,700 daN at 270 to 295 bar and up to 260 L/min, well above the SE series, and SRD E150 to G230 are built on request. The [SE series winch](/p/dinamic-oil-se-series-hydraulic-winches) is the nearest alternative; see our [hydraulic winches shelf](/c/hydraulic-winches).
